correctness.rationale: The exact one-update mutant-count drift gives a four-term two-step commutator. All six state cases with 2<=N<=4 are rational identities verified by symbolic expansion and a separately coded exact-rational transition matrix. The only sign-uncertain numerator has positive-coefficient substitutions when fitnesses are on one side of 1, and when a>1>b it is strictly increasing in b from negative at zero to positive at one. Thus the threshold exists uniquely and is sharp; 498 checker assertions passed.

value.rationale: The minimal population size at which opposing deterministic selection environments reverse the two-step expected-mutant-count ordering is a motivated finite-population genetics boundary. The theorem solves all states for N<=4 uniformly in two fitness variables, supplies a unique continuous fitness-phase threshold, and proves both strict sides with exact positive/negative rational examples. This structural drift-versus-selection effect is not reducible to a sign or normalization check; the narrow two-step scope and absence of broader demographic claims are explicit.
